text: What if one ant doubled every minute?
formula: Title question word for word (STANDARD 1.3); the rate is in the title (STANDARD 0.13). Count after n minutes = 2^n. Ant mass m = 2 mg (a common garden ant: 'the common ants which live in British gardens weigh about 1mg or 2mg', Prof. Francis Ratnieks, BBC News 2014; workers 1-5 mg, Wilson & Hoelldobler). Weight after n minutes = 2^n x 2e-6 kg. Pile size assumes ants about as dense as water (1,000 kg/m3): hemisphere radius r = (3 M / (2 pi rho))^(1/3); in space a ball r = (3 M / (4 pi rho))^(1/3).

text: One ant crashes your quiet picnic.
formula: Opening wish/problem (STANDARD 0.14). Paid off by n16.

text: Real ants need six weeks to grow.
formula: LEAN + reality first (STANDARD 2.11): 'The total life cycle of an ant, from egg to adult, can take six to 10 weeks' (UGA CAES Field Report, Ant biology).

text: This one doubles every minute. In two hours, it outweighs the Sun.
formula: SNAPBACK: Sun 1.989e30 kg / 2e-6 kg = 9.95e35 ants = 2^119.6 -> minute 120 = exactly 2 hours: 2^120 = 1.33e36 ants = 2.66e30 kg > 1.989e30 kg.

text: You could flick it away. You say one ant is fine.
formula: Blame + thread setup (STANDARD 2.3, 2.6); on screen your bubble 'ONE ANT IS FINE.' Paid off by n16.

text: Each minute, every ant becomes two.
Seventeen minutes. They outweigh your sandwich.
Now they outweigh Mittens. He is not impressed.
formula: Minute 22: 2^22 = 4,194,304 ants = 8.4 kg > Mittens, a typical 4.5 kg house cat (2^21 = 4.2 kg < 4.5 kg). Joke from the screen: Mittens' unimpressed face.

text: Now they outweigh you. One ant was fine, you said.
formula: Minute 26: 2^26 = 67,108,864 ants = 134 kg > you at 75 kg (2^25 = 67 kg < 75 kg). Blame callback to n4.

text: Half an hour. Heavier than an elephant.
formula: Minute 32 (about half an hour): 2^32 = 4.29 billion ants = 8,590 kg > a 6,000 kg African elephant bull (2^31 = 4,295 kg < 6,000). Next: minute 37: 2^37 = 137 billion = 275 t > a 150 t blue whale (NOAA: up to ~150 t / 330,000 lb). Pile r: elephant 1.6 m, whale 5.1 m.
Minute 43: 2^43 = 8.80 trillion ants = 17,600 t > Eiffel Tower 10,100 t total (2^42 = 8,800 t < 10,100). Pile r = 20 m.

text: More ants than every ant on Earth.
formula: Schultheiss et al. 2022, PNAS: about 20 quadrillion (2e16) ants on Earth. 2^54 = 1.8e16 < 2e16 < 2^55 = 3.6e16 -> minute 55.

text: They outweigh all eight billion humans.
formula: Human biomass ~0.06 Gt carbon (Bar-On et al. 2018, PNAS) ~ 400 million t wet mass (8 billion x ~50 kg average incl. children). Minute 58: 2^58 = 2.88e17 ants = 576 million t > 400 million t (2^57 = 288 million t < 400). Pile r = 650 m.

text: So heavy, its own gravity pulls it round.
formula: Bodies bigger than a few hundred km across are pulled round by their own gravity (e.g. Ceres, 940 km). Minute 90: 2^90 = 1.24e27 ants = 2.5e21 kg > all the oceans, 1.4e21 kg (1.335 billion km3 x 1,025 kg/m3; 2^89 = 1.24e21 < 1.4e21); ball radius (3 x 2.5e18/(4 pi))^(1/3) = 839 km. Minute 95: 2^95 = 7.9e22 kg > the Moon, 7.342e22 kg (2^94 = 3.96e22 < 7.34e22).

text: A hundred and two minutes. Heavier than Earth.
Two hours. Heavier than the Sun.
formula: Minute 120 = 2 h: 2^120 = 1.33e36 ants = 2.66e30 kg > Sun 1.989e30 kg (2^119 = 1.33e30 < 1.989e30). Ball radius (3 x 2.66e27/(4 pi))^(1/3) = 859,000 km vs the Sun's 696,000 km. Counter keeps doubling to minute 126 on the last frame.

text: Well. You did say one ant was fine.
formula: Callback ending (pays off n4 and the quiet-picnic wish), said while the counter keeps climbing.
